summary: Count to 100 from any number, count back from 20, count up to 30 objects and group them by tens.
Read and write numbers to 30, match them to groups, and compare amounts as more, fewer or the same.
Make and break apart numbers to 10, know partners of 5 and 10, and solve join and take-away stories.
Compare two things by length, height, weight, how much they hold, or how long they take.
Name, describe, draw and build circles, triangles, squares and rectangles, whichever way they face.
Know the days of the week and months of the year, and say yesterday, today and tomorrow.
Sort objects, ask a question, collect answers and read simple object and picture graphs.
Find the part that repeats in a pattern, continue it, and make your own repeating patterns.
Count to 120 from any number, back from 30, skip-count by 2s, 5s and 10s, and count like coins.
Read and write numbers to 120, show them as tens and ones, estimate, compare and order them.
Share a whole fairly into halves or fourths, using shapes and small sets of objects.
Know add and subtract facts to 10 by heart, solve problems within 20, and use = as a balance.
Measure length, weight and how much a container holds with non-standard units, and compare.
Describe, sort and draw circles, triangles, squares and rectangles, and join them into bigger shapes.
Tell time to the hour and half hour, and use a calendar to find days and dates.
Collect and sort data, then show and read it in object graphs, picture graphs and tables.
Continue and create repeating and growing patterns, and show one pattern in a different form.
Skip-count by 2s, 5s, 10s, 25s and 100s, count back by 10s, estimate, and tell odd from even.
Read, write, compare and order three-digit numbers, and place numbers to 100 on a number line.
Name and write halves, thirds, fourths, sixths and eighths, count unit fractions and compare them.
Count coins and dollar bills up to $2, make amounts, and write them with ¢ and $.
Know facts to 20 by heart, estimate, add and subtract within 100, and solve one- and two-step stories.
Estimate and measure length in inches, weight in pounds and liquid in cups, with the right tool.
Tell time to the nearest 5 minutes and pick sensible units of time for an activity.
Find and draw lines of symmetry, and see the two halves match in shape and size.
Compare flat and solid shapes: count faces, edges and corners of cubes, boxes and spheres.
Collect data, then make and read picture graphs with a key and bar graphs.
Continue, create and retell repeating and growing patterns, including adding number patterns.
Read and write numbers up to six digits in standard, expanded and word form, and name each digit's value.
Compare and order whole numbers up to 9,999 using >, <, = and ≠.
Show, name, compare and find equal fractions and mixed numbers with models and on number lines.
Count, compare and make up amounts of money to $5, and make change by counting on.
Estimate, add and subtract within 1,000, and solve one- and two-step story problems.
Know times and division facts to 10 × 10 by heart, and solve one-step multiplying and dividing stories.
Estimate and measure length, weight and liquid volume in customary and metric units.
Find area by counting square units and perimeter by adding the sides of a polygon.
Tell time to the minute and solve elapsed-time problems in whole hours.
Name and sort polygons up to octagons, and put shapes together or cut them apart.
Collect data, make and read scaled picture and bar graphs, and solve problems with them.
Continue and create growing and shrinking number patterns, and find missing terms.
Read and write whole numbers up to nine digits and name the value of each digit.
Compare and order whole numbers up to seven digits.
Compare, order and find equal fractions and mixed numbers, and see a fraction as a division.
Read, write, compare and order decimals to thousandths, and name each digit's value.
Write halves, fourths, fifths, tenths and hundredths as decimals, and decimals as fractions.
Estimate by rounding, and add and subtract whole numbers with the standard method.
Know facts to 12 × 12, find factors, multiply up to 2 × 2 digits and divide by one digit.
Add and subtract fractions and mixed numbers with like denominators, and multiply a whole by a unit fraction.
Add and subtract decimals to thousandths, and solve story problems with them.
Pick sensible units, measure length, weight and liquid volume, and convert customary units.
Solve elapsed-time problems in hours and minutes, including across a.m. and p.m.
Use formulas for the area and perimeter of rectangles and squares, and solve problems.
Name and draw points, lines, segments, rays and angles, and spot parallel and perpendicular lines.
Sort quadrilaterals like rhombi and trapezoids by their sides and right angles.
Name solid shapes like cones and pyramids, and compare them with flat shapes by faces and edges.
Collect data, make and read line graphs, and solve problems using them.
Describe chances as impossible to certain, list outcomes, and write a probability as a fraction.
Find the rule in number patterns and input/output tables, and extend them.
Switch between fractions and decimals, and compare and order mixed sets of fractions and decimals.
Tell prime from composite numbers up to 100 and find a number's prime factorization.
Estimate and solve multi-step whole-number problems with all four operations, including remainders.
Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators, and multiply a whole number by a fraction.
Estimate, add, subtract, multiply and divide decimals, and solve story problems with them.
Simplify expressions with the order of operations, including one set of parentheses.
Pick and use metric units for length, mass and liquid volume, and convert between them.
Find the area of right triangles and the volume of boxes, and choose perimeter, area or volume.
Sort angles and triangles, measure angles, and use the 180° triangle sum to find a missing angle.
Collect data, make and read line plots and stem-and-leaf plots, and solve problems with them.
Find the mean, median, mode and range of a data set and use them to answer questions.
List all outcomes with a tree diagram or table, count them by multiplying, and find a probability.
Find rules in patterns with whole numbers, fractions and decimals, and extend them.
Use a letter or box for an unknown, and write one-step equations and expressions from words.
